# Pavāraṇākkhandhaka (Kd 4)

**ID:** Kd 4
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Pavāraṇākkhandhaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The chapter on the invitation ceremony
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd4
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pavāraṇākkhandhaka* ("The chapter on the invitation ceremony") is the fourth chapter of the Khandhaka division of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Frauwallner 1956]. It sets out the rules governing the *pavāraṇā* ceremony, a compulsory annual assembly held at the conclusion of the rains retreat (*vassāvāsa*) wherein monastics formally invite mutual correction and admonition from their peers regarding seen, heard, or suspected offenses [SuttaCentral; Banerjee 1979]. The text opens at Sāvatthī in the Jetavana monastery, where monks assemble to meet the Buddha after their rains residence; upon inquiring into their conduct, the Buddha lays down the procedural framework for the invitation ceremony, including exemptions, postponement, and penalties for non-compliance [Banerjee 1979]. Alongside the preceding *Uposathakkhandhaka*, this chapter is recognized as one of the two primary sections in the Vinaya that examine the formal mechanics and validity of monastic legal acts (*saṅghakamma*) in exhaustive detail [Sujato 2009].

Curated parallels recorded by SuttaCentral include the *Pravāraṇāvastu* of various Vinaya recensions, surviving in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese translations of the Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka lineages, as well as related material in the Mahāsaṅghika tradition [SuttaCentral; Frauwallner 1956; Banerjee 1979]. Automatically computed matches in DharmaNexus align the Pali text directly with the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (*'dul ba gzhi*) [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus records widespread text reuse (nearly 16,000 matches across 196 texts), sharing extensive procedural formulas particularly with the *Uposathakkhandhaka* (Kd 2) and *Pārivāsikakkhandhaka* (Kd 12), as well as subcommentaries including the *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Modern translations include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
